The patient is lying down, with monitoring leads and medical equipment visible, suggesting a hospital setting. The skin lesions are prominent and consistent with a systemic dermatologic or infectious process.

Case_20001/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Legs, appearance at presentation with diffuse papulonodular lesions

description.short_caption: Diffuse papulonodular lesions on both legs at presentation.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows both legs of a patient with numerous papulonodular lesions distributed diffusely across the skin. The lesions vary in size and appear darkly pigmented or crusted in some areas. The surrounding skin shows no overt erythema or swelling. The patient is partially covered with a white sheet, and the lesions are most prominent on the anterior and lateral aspects of the legs.

Case_20001/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Histoplasmosis, GMS stain 40x: Highlighting many oval-shaped uniform fungal yeasts, morphologically consistent with Histoplasma.

description.short_caption: GMS stain showing numerous oval fungal yeasts, consistent with Histoplasma.
description.detailed_description: This image is a GMS (Gomori methenamine silver) stain at 40x magnification. It highlights numerous oval-shaped, uniform fungal yeasts, which are darkly stained black against a green background. The organisms are morphologically consistent with Histoplasma species. The stain enhances the visibility of fungal cell walls, aiding in the identification of fungal pathogens.

Case_20001/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Histoplasmosis, H&E stain 40x: Numerous intracytoplasmic yeast forms are present inside histiocytes

description.short_caption: Histoplasmosis, H&E stain 40x: Numerous intracytoplasmic yeast forms inside histiocytes.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained section at 40x magnification. Numerous small, round to oval yeast forms are visible within the cytoplasm of histiocytes. The yeast forms are uniform in size and are surrounded by a clear halo, consistent with a fungal infection. The background shows inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and macrophages, indicative of a granulomatous response.
visible_findings: histiocytes with clear halos around yeast
